faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Countersunk Screw (ISO 10642) suitable for Countersunk flat head screw for flush mounting?
faq.a: Titanium Countersunk Screw (ISO 10642) uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address fastener operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Countersunk Screw (ISO 10642)?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Countersunk Screw (ISO 10642) is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for countersunk flat head requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Countersunk Screw (ISO 10642) require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. countersunk flat head components require Passivation per ASTM B600 followed by hot DI water rinse 70C minimum to prevent flash rust on finished surfaces — tailored for countersunk flat head application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.
